verses.38:2: Eu disse: {custodiam} os meus caminhos, * para não {delinquam} {inlingua2}.
verses.38:2b: Pus {custodia} à minha boca, * quando o pecador {consisteret} contra mim.
verses.38:3: Emudeci, e fui humilhado, e fiquei em silêncio {abonis}: * e a minha dor se renovou.
verses.38:4: O meu coração {concaluit} dentro de mim: * e na minha meditação {exardescet}.
verses.38:5b: E qual é o número dos meus dias: * para que eu saiba o que me falta.
verses.38:6: Eis que {mensurabiles} os meus dias: * e {substantia6} é como nada diante de vós.
verses.38:6b: {verumtamen6}, tudo é vaidade, * todo homem que vive.
verses.38:7: {verumtamen7}, o homem passa {imagine}: * mas também em vão se perturba.
verses.38:8: E agora, {exspectatio} Não é o Senhor? * E {substantia8} está {apud8}.
verses.38:10: Emudeci, e não abri a minha boca, {fecisti}: * afastai de mim {plagas}.
verses.38:12: {fortitudine} da vossa mão eu desfaleci nas repreensões: * por causa da iniquidade castigastes o homem.
verses.38:12b: E fizestes a sua alma definhar como uma aranha: * {verumtamen12}, em vão se perturba todo homem.
verses.38:13b: Não fiqueis em silêncio: porque eu sou {advena} {apud13}, e {peregrinus}, * como todos os meus pais.
verses.38:14: {remitte}, para que eu {refrigerer} antes de partir, * {nonero}.

decisions.latin: Custódiam vias meas … Pósui ori meo custódiam
decisions.why: The Latin sounds one word twice in two cola: *custódiam* the verb (I will guard) and *custódiam* the noun (a guard) — in the Greek too, φυλάξω … φυλακήν. custodíre → guardar (glossary); its noun is *guarda*, so the echo survives: *Guardarei os meus caminhos … Pus guarda à minha boca*. *pôr guarda a* without the article is Matos Soares 1932's wording and a living idiom. The custodíre row records that *guardar caminhos* left one blind reader unsure (followed? watched?); here the next colon says what the guarding is for. MS1932 *Velarei sobre o meu proceder* loses both the ways and the echo. The two cola are quoted in the Rule of St Benedict, ch. 6 (DO Regula/01-24, grep), and 38:2b is a versicle (Sancti/Bavaria 05-16); 140:3 *Pone, Dómine, custódiam ori meo* should copy the noun.

options.label: Guardarei … guarda
options.note: Ruling: the root twice, as the Latin and the Greek.

options.label: Guardarei … uma guarda
options.note: The article supplied; heavier, a sentry more than a watch.

options.label: Velarei sobre … guarda
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's verb; breaks the echo.

decisions.latin: ut non delínquam in lingua mea
decisions.why: delínquere → cometer faltas (row; 18:13, 24:7, 33:22 kept it apart from peccáre → pecar). Here the Greek is ἁμαρτάνειν, the verb behind peccáre, and Douay-Rheims / Matos Soares 1932 both write 'sin' — but the Latin chose delínquere, and the row keeps the Latin's two verbs two. The final infinitive after *para não* is the Portuguese build when the subject is the same (118:60).

options.label: pecar
options.note: The Greek's verb, DRB, MS1932; peccáre's word in this psalter.

decisions.why: *in lingua mea* twice in four verses: the instrument (ἐν γλώσσῃ, the Hebrew בִלְשֹׁונִי). Portuguese says the instrument with *com* (Douay-Rheims 'with my tongue', Matos Soares 1932 'com a minha língua' both times); *na minha língua* is heard as 'in my language'. One wording for both places, as the Latin has one.

options.label: na minha língua
options.note: The preposition kept; heard as 'in my language'.

decisions.why: consístere: to take one's stand, take up a position (L&S; in law, to appear as accuser against). συστῆναι … ἐναντίον μου. Douay-Rheims 'stood against me', Matos Soares 1932 'se apresentava contra mim'. *postar-se* is exactly taking a position; *levantar-se* and *pôr-se* are spoken for (insúrgere / exsúrgere, astáre). 26:3 *Si consístant … castra* took *se instalar* (a camp); a person stands. v2: *se postava* was stiff to the stylist and unknown to the blind reader; *se erguia* taken.

options.label: se erguia
options.note: Ruling (v2): the stylist's plain verb of standing up; *postava* was unknown to the blind reader. erguer-se is also one of astáre's words, but the two never meet in a verse.

decisions.why: silére → ficar em silêncio (row; 34:22 and 38:13b *ne síleas* → *não fiqueis em silêncio*). *a bonis* (ἐξ ἀγαθῶν) is open: kept silent even about good things, or silent and cut off from good things. Douay-Rheims 'kept silence from good things' keeps both; Matos Soares 1932 'nem mesmo falei de coisas boas' chooses the first. Portuguese has no 'silent from'; *sobre coisas boas* is the nearer reading and the one both witnesses lean to. bona → *coisas boas* (12:6b row) — *os bens* would be heard as property. v2: the Latinist (minor) read *a bonis* as separative and refused *sobre* (it makes the good things the topic); the stylist also refused *sobre coisas boas* (a topic of conversation) and found the colon breathless. Both asked for *calar-se* (*calei-me das coisas boas*, *calei-me acerca do bem*), which is tacére's verb (the silére / tacére row, 27:1) and would break the echo with 38:13b *Não fiqueis em silêncio*. The separative taken with *longe de*, the psalter's way of saying the separating *a* (30:21, 30:12b). v3 (the gate, minor): *longe do bem* makes a spatial sense the Latin lacks and turns the plural into an abstract; *quanto às coisas boas* leaves both readings open, which is what D2 asks. Taken; it costs the stylist's brevity (the colon is +8) and has a faint register of paperwork.

options.label: quanto às coisas boas
options.note: Ruling (v3): the Latinist's gate fix — leaves open whether the good things were withheld or not spoken of, and keeps the plural *bona*.

options.label: longe do bem
options.note: Draft 2. Ruling (v2): the separative *a*, as 30:21 and 30:12b (*longe de*); *bona* as the abstract *o bem* (as univérsa → *tudo*), which also shortens the colon.

options.label: sobre coisas boas
options.note: Draft 1. Ruling: silent about good things.

decisions.latin: Concáluit cor meum intra me: et in meditatióne mea exardéscet ignis
decisions.why: Two verbs of heat, a perfect then a future (ἐθερμάνθη … ἐκκαυθήσεται, the same tenses). concaléscere is to grow thoroughly warm (L&S); exardéscere → inflamar-se (row, 117:12). Matos Soares 1932 has *inflamou-se … acendiam-se*, which spends the row's verb on the first and makes the future a past; Douay-Rheims keeps the future ('a fire shall flame out'). The future is the Latin's: the fire is still coming. v2: the blind reader heard *O meu coração se aqueceu* as 'my heart was warmed (comforted)'; *ardeu* taken.

options.label: ardeu … um fogo se inflamará
options.note: Ruling (v2): the blind reader heard *se aqueceu* as 'was comforted' — the heat of distress was lost. *ardeu* keeps the heat and stays apart from inflamar-se.

options.label: se aqueceu … um fogo se inflamará
options.note: Draft 1. Ruling: two verbs, the tenses kept.

options.label: se aqueceu … se acendia um fogo

decisions.latin: Notum fac mihi, Dómine, finem meum
decisions.why: 15:11 *Notas mihi fecísti vias vitæ* → *Fizestes-me conhecer os caminhos da vida*: the same build, so the same verb. Matos Soares 1932 'Faze-me conhecer'.

mensurábilis: that can be measured (L&S). The Greek is παλαιστάς, 'handbreadths' (the Hebrew's image); the Latin has made it 'measurable', and the Latin is followed. The pónere + predicate row: the Portuguese build's verb (*tornar*), as 17:33. Matos Soares 1932 'puseste os meus dias em medida' keeps *pôr*, and Douay-Rheims 'made my days measurable'. v2: *mensuráveis* unknown to the blind reader, a technical Latinism to the stylist; Matos Soares 1932's *pusestes em medida* taken.

options.label: pusestes em medida
options.note: Ruling (v2): the Latin's verb and the idea of measure in a plain noun; *mensuráveis* was unknown to the blind reader and 'technical' to the stylist.

options.label: fizestes do tamanho de um palmo

forms.mensurabiles: fizestes do tamanho de um palmo

options.note: The Greek and Hebrew image; not the Latin.

options.label: fizestes medidos
options.note: The stylist's; a calque of pónere + predicate (17:33's fault).

decisions.why: *substántia mea* twice (ὑπόστασις both times): what the man is, his being, set against nothing (38:6) and found with God (38:8). One wording for both. *a minha substância* is the calque (Douay-Rheims) and in Portuguese is chemistry or philosophy; *o meu ser* is Matos Soares 1932 in 38:6 (in 38:8 he has *todos os meus bens*, which is 108:11's sense — property — not this one). New row proposed; 88:48 *quæ mea substántia* and 138:15 can follow, 108:11 (property) and 68:3 (*non est substántia*, footing) decide locally.

verúmtamen → todavia (row, open; 31:6b, 90:8). Three times here, so the Portuguese says one word three times. The Greek has πλήν, μέντοιγε, πλήν — often asseverative ('surely'), and Douay-Rheims reads 'And indeed … Surely … surely'; Matos Soares 1932 'Ah! sim … Sim … Sim'. But the Latin word is adversative ('but yet'), and in each place it turns against what went before (my being is nothing before you — yet all is vanity; he wastes away — yet all men fret in vain). *Na verdade* is the option that follows the asseverative reading.

ἐν εἰκόνι: man passes 'in an image' — as a mere likeness, a shadow of reality. Douay-Rheims 'as an image'; Matos Soares 1932 'como uma sombra' (another word). *em imagem* keeps the preposition and is not Portuguese; *como uma imagem* is the plain build of the Latin's sense and keeps the word *imagem*. imágo also 72:20. Gate (v2, minor, repeated from v1): *como* settles a phrase the tradition also reads as 'in the image (of God)'. Held: *passa em imagem* is not a Portuguese sentence, and a prayed line must be one; the reader of the Latin column sees *in imágine*. Option 2 is his wording.

One verb, a colon to itself (θησαυρίζει). *Entesoura* is the verb of the same root (Matos Soares 1932) and current. The thesáurus row (32:7 *depósitos*, because *tesouros* was heard as riches) is about storehouses of nature; here riches are the sense. *Acumula* (plainer) loses the treasure. v2: see the Latinist's *os* and the blind reader's unknown *Entesoura*; *Acumula tesouros* taken.

options.label: Acumula tesouros
options.note: Ruling (v2): *Entesoura* was unknown to the blind reader, who could not hear its subject or what *os* stood for; the Latinist marked *os* as dangling. A noun gives *os* its antecedent (the treasures = *ea*).

options.label: Ajunta tesouros
options.note: The stylist's; *ajunta … juntará* would make one verb of thesaurizáre and congregáre.

decisions.why: ignoráre with a question after it: 'does not know for whom'. 34:8 *quem ignórat* → *que desconhece* and 34:11 *quæ ignorábam* → *o que eu desconhecia* took *desconhecer* with a noun object; with an indirect question Portuguese says *não sabe* (34:15 *et ignorávi* → *e eu não soube*, the Latinist's word there). congregáre → juntar (32:7, 34:15); *ea* (neuter plural, 'these things') → *os*, the treasures of *Entesoura*.

decisions.latin: Et nunc quæ est exspectátio mea? Nonne Dóminus?
decisions.why: exspectátio → *o que aguardo* (row, D24, D36: *aguardar* is exspectáre's; *expectativa* failed the stylist as bureaucratic; 118:116 *pelo que aguardo*). The noun becomes a clause (grammar): *que é que eu aguardo? Não é o Senhor?* The answer still names what is awaited. Greek ὑπομονή. Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932 'hope / esperança' — spes's word, refused under D36. v2: the Latinist (minor) and the stylist ('que é que' is filler) both asked for *qual é a minha espera?*. Taken: *espera* is the noun of waiting, the plain one the row lacked (*expectativa* bureaucratic, *o que aguardo* a clause). It shares the root of *esperar* (D36's cost, again); proposed on the row.

options.label: qual é a minha espera?
options.note: Ruling (v2): the noun, as the Latinist and the stylist both asked. *espera* is waiting, not hope; the verbs stay apart (D36), this is exspectátio's noun where it stands as subject.

decisions.latin: substántia mea apud te est … ádvena ego sum apud te
decisions.why: apud te → junto de vós (row; 21:26, 35:10). Twice here, so the same words twice. In 38:8 the Greek has παρὰ σοῦ ('from you'), and the row follows the Latin's *apud* (Douay-Rheims 'with thee'); in 38:13b παρὰ σοί ('with you'), and Douay-Rheims 'with thee', Matos Soares 1932 'diante de ti'.

decisions.latin: Ab ómnibus iniquitátibus meis érue me
decisions.why: éruere with a source → arrancar (row; 21:21, 31:7 *arrancai-me dos que me cercam*, 36:40). Without a source the row gives *libertar* (24:20, D37 review). Here the source is named. The Portuguese order puts the verb first (natural order, D2).

options.label: Libertai-me
options.note: The source-less form; MS1932 'Livra-me' is liberáre's.

decisions.why: *dare* + a predicate noun (ἔδωκάς με ὄνειδος ἄφρονι): you made me a reproach to the fool. oppróbrium → afronta (row); insípiens → insensato (row). Douay-Rheims 'thou hast made me a reproach to the fool', Matos Soares 1932 'tu me fizeste um objecto de opróbrio para o insensato'. The pónere + predicate row: the Portuguese build's verb. Keeping *dar* (*me destes como afronta ao insensato*) makes 'afronta ao insensato' heard as an insult offered TO the fool; *para* keeps the fool as the one who scorns. v2: the blind reader could not tell the direction of *afronta para o insensato*; the stylist asked for a genitive (*o opróbrio do insensato*). The genitive taken with the row's noun. Gate (v2, minor): he wants the dative and *dar* back (*destes-me como afronta ao insensato*) — on draft 1 he had passed *para o insensato*. Held: *afronta ao insensato* is heard as an insult offered to the fool, and the blind reader could not tell the direction with *para*; the genitive says whose scorn it is. His wording is the option.

options.label: fizestes de mim a afronta do insensato

forms.dedisti: fizestes de mim a afronta do insensato

options.note: Ruling (v2): the genitive (the stylist) — the fool is the one who scorns, which *para o* left unclear to the blind reader; afronta kept (the row: *opróbrio* failed two readers).

options.label: fizestes de mim uma afronta para o insensato

forms.dedisti: fizestes de mim uma afronta para o insensato

options.label: me destes como afronta ao insensato

forms.dedisti: me destes como afronta ao insensato

options.note: The verb kept; the dative ambiguous.

decisions.why: fecísti has no object in the Latin: 'because you did (it)'. The Greek has ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ ποιήσας με, 'you are the one who made me' — the Latin does not. Portuguese needs an object pronoun: *o* (Douay-Rheims 'thou hast done it', Matos Soares 1932 'tu o fizeste'). *tu* is emphatic, so *vós* is said.

options.label: porque fostes vós que o fizestes

forms.fecisti: porque fostes vós que o fizestes

options.note: The emphasis made a cleft; longer.

options.label: porque vós me fizestes
options.note: The Greek's 'made me' — not the Latin.

decisions.why: plaga is a blow, a stroke; its Greek here is μάστιγας, the same word behind flagélla (31:10, 34:15 → *os flagelos*). By D15's test (one Greek word, no difference of sense) the Portuguese may be one: *os vossos flagelos* (Matos Soares 1932; Douay-Rheims 'thy scourges'). The blind reader of Ps 34 did not know *flagelos* (heard calamities); *golpes* is plain and is plaga's own sense. amovére → afastar (row; 118:29 *Afastai de mim*).

options.label: os vossos flagelos
options.note: Ruling: one Greek word, one Portuguese.

decisions.latin: A fortitúdine manus tuæ ego deféci in increpatiónibus
decisions.why: *a* + ablative (ἀπὸ τῆς ἰσχύος): by, from the strength of your hand. fortitúdo → força (row); defícere → desfalecer (row, a person fainting — not the 'is gone' of 11:2); increpátio → repreensão (17:16b). *Pela força* keeps the cause; Matos Soares 1932 'Debaixo da força' makes it a place. The DO pointing puts *in increpatiónibus* with *deféci*, against the Greek's verse division; the Latin is followed.

decisions.latin: Exáudi oratiónem meam, Dómine, et deprecatiónem meam
decisions.why: D3 escutar, D35 prece, D4 *dar ouvidos a* in the second colon (as 53:4, 5:2, 16:1b). The Latin puts the vocative between the two objects; Portuguese can keep that order, and it lets the two nouns be heard as two (*a minha oração … e a minha prece*). The colon is a versicle for St Benedict Joseph Labre (Sancti/aliquibus locis/04-16, grep); and the Matins versicle *Deus, ne síleas a me, remítte mihi* and a responsory (Epi2-2) join 38:13–14 with 27:1.

options.label: Escutai a minha oração, Senhor, e a minha prece

forms.exaudi: Escutai a minha oração, Senhor, e a minha prece

options.label: Escutai, Senhor, a minha oração e a minha prece

forms.exaudi: Escutai, Senhor, a minha oração e a minha prece

decisions.latin: quóniam ádvena ego sum apud te, et peregrínus
decisions.why: ádvena here is πάροικος — the Greek behind íncola in 118:19 *Íncola ego sum in terra* → *Eu sou forasteiro na terra*. The íncola row said 'kept apart from ádvena' before the Greek was checked; by D15's test the two may share *forasteiro*, and the prayer is then heard as the same confession. peregrínus (παρεπίδημος, one staying a while) → *peregrino* (Matos Soares 1932, Douay-Rheims 'sojourner'); 68:9 will follow. *estrangeiro* is the option (alienus → estranho already). 93:6, 145:9 (ádvena, the stranger in the land) decide in their psalms.

options.label: adventício … peregrino
options.note: Matos Soares 1932; the cognate, unknown to most.

decisions.why: remíttere + dative, no object: 'forgive me' (Douay-Rheims 'O forgive me'), or 'let up on me, give me respite' — the Greek ἄνες μοι is the second (relax, let go). The Latin word is remíttere, which this psalter has as *perdoar* (31:1 *remíssæ sunt iniquitátes*); Matos Soares 1932 'Deixa que eu tome algum alento' paraphrases the respite. The Latin leaves it open; *Perdoai-me* is its commonest sense and the Vulgate-family reading. Gate (v2, minor): *Perdoai-me* keeps only 'forgive'; *Relevai-me* would keep both. Held: *relevar alguém* is uncommon, and the blind reader heard 'relent' as a second sense of *Perdoai-me* already. Option 2.

options.label: Relevai-me
options.note: The gate's proposal: *relevar* holds both 'pardon' and 'relieve'. Rare with a person as object in Brazil.

decisions.why: refrigeráre: to cool, to refresh (L&S); ἀναψύξω, to cool, revive, get one's breath back. *tomar alento* (Matos Soares 1932) is to get one's breath and strength back — the Greek's sense and the Latin's. *ser refrescado* (Douay-Rheims 'refreshed') is heard as physical cooling; *refrigério* (65:12, the refection row) was unknown to a blind reader. v2: the Latinist (minor) asked for the passive, *seja reanimado*; *alento* unknown to the blind reader. Taken; and *antes que eu parta* → *antes de partir* (the stylist: 'que eu' twice in one colon).

options.label: seja reanimado
options.note: Ruling (v2): the Latin's passive (the Latinist); *alento* was unknown to the blind reader.

options.label: encontre refrigério
options.note: The Church's noun; a verb supplied.

decisions.why: *ero* absolute: I shall not be any more (οὐκέτι μὴ ὑπάρξω). The Latin is an independent future, not governed by *priúsquam*. *e não serei mais* is the bare verb and hangs in Portuguese ('not be more — what?'); *existir* is what *esse* means when it stands alone. Matos Soares 1932 'e deixe de existir' puts it under 'before'.

options.label: e não existirei mais
options.note: ámplius as *mais*; rhymes with *pais* at the end of 38:13b (checks).

options.label: e não serei mais
options.note: The bare verb (DRB 'be no more'); the same rhyme.

choices.38:2: Dixi → *Eu disse* (the subject named; DRB 'I said'). via → caminho (row).
choices.38:3: obmutéscere → *emudecer*, the same word in 38:10 (the only two places, grep). humiliátus sum → *fui humilhado* (118:107). renováre → *renovar-se*. First colon +8 in v3 (*quanto às coisas boas*, the gate's fix): three verbs, and silére takes the row's two-word *ficar em silêncio* (kept, so that 38:13b and 34:22 are heard with it); accepted.
choices.38:9: Draft 1 *uma afronta para o insensato* (+4); v2 the genitive, shorter. iníquitas → iniquidade.
choices.38:5b: scire with an indirect question → *saber* (the scire row: collocation leads). desse → *faltar* (22:1 *nada me faltará*).
choices.38:6: Ecce → *Eis que* (row). ante te → *diante de vós*.
choices.38:6b: *univérsa* (neuter plural, τὰ σύμπαντα) → *tudo*; *omnis homo vivens* in apposition → *todo homem que vive*. vánitas → vaidade (row).
choices.38:7: frustra (38:7) and vane (38:12b) are one Greek word (μάτην) → *em vão* both, and *conturbátur* → *se perturba* both (conturbáre row), so 38:12b answers 38:7. *sed et* → *mas também*.
choices.38:10: Emudeci as in 38:3. aperíre → abrir (the first person, no ban).
choices.38:13: áuribus pércipe → *dai ouvidos a* (D4 names 38:13). lácrimæ → lágrimas (row) — a proparoxytone at the final, where the Latin ends on *meas*; no plain word avoids it, and the possessive after the noun would be inversion for its own sake. First colon −5: the Latin's long words.
choices.38:13b: *Ne síleas* → *Não fiqueis em silêncio*, as 34:22 and 27:1. *ego sum* → *eu sou*. patres → pais.
choices.38:14: priúsquam ábeam → *antes de partir* (v2, the stylist: *antes que eu parta* doubled *que eu*; same subject, so the infinitive). The Latin's *ero* stays independent: *e já não existirei*.
choices.38:12b: tabéscere → definhar (row; 118:139 *me fez definhar*). *sicut aráneam* → *como uma aranha* (DRB 'like a spider'), left where it may go with the soul or with the wasting, as the Latin. The finals of 38:12 and 38:12b both end on *homem*: the Latin has the same word at both ends (*hóminem … homo*), so the echo is kept.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm38.txt, 18 prayed verses (38:2–38:14 with 38:2b, 5b, 6b, 7b, 12b, 13b; no 38:1, the titulus, D7; DO has no 38:11 — its Latin is joined to 38:10 and 38:12). No flex. Uses by grep (ps032/uses.py): 38:2–3 quoted in the Rule of St Benedict ch. 6 (Regula/01-24); 38:2, 38:2b versicles and a short responsory for St John Nepomuk (Sancti/Bavaria/05-16); 38:4 an Alleluia verse (missa Sancti/05-26); 38:13 a versicle for St Benedict Joseph Labre (Sancti/aliquibus locis/04-16); the Matins versicle *Deus, ne síleas a me, remítte mihi* and the responsory Epi2-2 join 38:13–14 to 27:1. Not in the Diurnal Monástico parallels. The Hetzenauer print read is skipped and owed.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps038.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Formulas checked with ps038/xref.py (the Latin of the finished psalms beside their Portuguese) and ps005/grep_latin.py: *ne síleas* = 34:22, 27:1; *áuribus pércipe* = D4; *Exáudi oratiónem meam* = 4:2b, 53:4; *Notum fac* ≈ 15:11; *ámove a me* = 118:29; *nihil déerit* 22:1; *érue* with a source 31:7, 36:40; *Humiliátus sum* 118:107; *tabéscere fecit* 118:139; *apud te* 21:26, 35:10; *íncola ego sum* 118:19; flagélla (μάστιγες) 31:10, 34:15. Rulings applied: D3, D4, D21, D24/D36 (exspectátio), D35. D37 and D38 have no place here (no *usque in ætérnum*, no *inops*). Latin readings kept against the Greek: 38:10 *quóniam tu fecísti* (not 'made me'), 38:6 *mensurábiles* (not 'handbreadths'), 38:14 *Remítte* as 'forgive'. Tests for the readers: 'guardar os meus caminhos', 'se postava', 'fiquei em silêncio sobre coisas boas', 'o meu ser', 'como uma imagem', 'Entesoura … os juntará', 'que é que eu aguardo?', 'fizestes de mim uma afronta para o insensato', 'flagelos', 'tome alento', 'não existirei mais'.

Draft 1: hard pass. 38:3 first colon +6 (three verbs, silére's two-word *ficar em silêncio*), 38:9 second +4 (*fazer de mim*), 38:2 second, 38:4 first, 38:5b second, 38:13b first, 38:14 first +3; 38:12 and 38:13 first −5 (the Latin's long words). 38:13 ends on the proparoxytone *lágrimas*. Rhyme 38:12 / 38:12b (*homem … homem*) kept: the Latin's own echo (*hóminem … homo*). The rhyme 38:13b / 38:14 (*pais … mais*) was mended before any reader: *e já não existirei*.

codex.py tried for the Latinist (critic/v1.latinist.json) and the ambiguity reader (critic/v1.ambiguity.json): both failed at once with 'Your workspace is out of credits'; not retried (Gustavo's instruction, Codex out of quota). The stylist is not run through Codex. All three v1 readers handed to the coordinator, to be run as fresh-context readers that see only the target file.

Draft 1, read by claude-opus-5-5 (fresh context; Codex out of credits). No major; five minors. «A faithful, close rendering of the Clementine Latin: Septuagintal readings (exardescet future, in imagine, a bonis, araneam, plagas) are kept, no Hebraizing, and the pointing matches the Latin in every verse.» Passed: cometer faltas, guarda, o meu ser, todavia ×3, junto de vós ×2, Arrancai-me, porque vós o fizestes, flagelos, Perdoai-me, e já não existirei.

outcomes.remark: minor: *a bonis* is separative; *sobre* makes the good things the topic → 'e calei-me das coisas boas'
outcomes.reason: In substance: the separative with *longe do bem* (30:21, 30:12b); his *calar-se* is tacére's verb and would break the echo with 38:13b; *sobre coisas boas* stays an option.

outcomes.remark: minor: *in imágine* is 'in', not 'as' → 'o homem passa em imagem'
outcomes.reason: *passa em imagem* is not Portuguese; *como* is the build the sense takes (DRB 'as an image'); his wording is option 2.

outcomes.remark: minor: masculine *os* dangles (ea neuter plural) → 'para quem juntará essas coisas'
outcomes.reason: Mended the other way: *Acumula tesouros* gives *os* its antecedent (the treasures are what *ea* means), which also answers the blind reader's unknown *Entesoura*.

outcomes.remark: minor: the noun recast as a clause → 'qual é a minha espera?'
minor: *refrígerer* is passive → 'para que eu seja reanimado'

audit.note: Draft 1, read by claude-opus-5-5 (fresh context; not run through Codex, by Gustavo's instruction). Nine verses; best 38:13, worst 38:3. «The psalm reads faithfully and mostly with dignity. The vós address sits naturally, and the three 'todavia' refrains give it a sober spine.» Six taken in whole or part, three refused.

outcomes.remark: 'cometer faltas' school register, slack → 'para não pecar com a minha língua'
outcomes.reason: *pecar* is peccáre's; delínquere → cometer faltas (row; 18:13, 24:7, 33:22). The Latinist passed it.

outcomes.remark: 'se postava' stiff, military → 'se erguia'
worst line: 'sobre coisas boas' a topic of conversation, colon breathless → 'e calei-me acerca do bem'
outcomes.reason: In part: *sobre* dropped and the colon shortened (*longe do bem*, the Latinist's separative); *calar-se* refused — tacére's verb (27:1), and 38:13b keeps *ficar em silêncio* for the same Latin.

outcomes.remark: 'mensuráveis' technical, 'tornastes' weak → 'fizestes medidos'
outcomes.reason: In substance, with Matos Soares 1932's *pusestes em medida* (the Latin's verb); his *fizestes medidos* is the calque of the pónere + predicate row's fault, kept as an option.

outcomes.remark: 'Entesoura' rare, subjectless → 'Ajunta tesouros'
outcomes.reason: In substance: *Acumula tesouros*; *Ajunta … juntará* would make one verb of thesaurizáre and congregáre. His wording is an option.

outcomes.remark: 'que é que' filler → 'qual é a minha espera?'
'uma afronta para o' prosaic → 'fizestes de mim o opróbrio do insensato'
outcomes.reason: The genitive taken; *opróbrio* refused — it failed two blind readers (oppróbrium row → afronta).

outcomes.remark: 'eu' adds a syllable, 'nas repreensões' trails → 'Sob a força … desfaleci'
outcomes.reason: *ego* is written in the Latin (emphatic), so *eu* stays; *Sob* makes a place of the cause (*a* + ablative); *Sob a força* is option 2. increpátio → repreensão (17:16b).

outcomes.remark: 'que eu' twice; 'existirei' abstract → 'antes de partir, * e já não serei'
outcomes.reason: In part: *antes de partir* taken; *e já não serei* refused — the bare *serei* hangs in Portuguese; *e não serei mais* is option 3.

audit.note: Draft 1, blind, read by claude-opus-5-5 (fresh context; Codex out of credits). 37 items, 7 unknown words (Entesoura, alento, mensuráveis, insensato, definhar, postava, flagelos) — four mended. Heard rightly or within the Latin's range: *Guardarei os meus caminhos* (be careful how I live), *Pus guarda à minha boca*, *e fui humilhado*, *o meu fim* (death, purpose second), *o que me falta* (what I lack — the Latin's *quid desit*), *o meu ser*, *mas também em vão se perturba*, *Não é o Senhor?* (rhetorical), *porque vós o fizestes* (you did it), *castigastes o homem*, *Perdoai-me* (forgive, 'relent' second — the Latin's range), *antes que eu parta* (before I die).

outcomes.remark: 'se aqueceu' heard as 'was comforted'
outcomes.reason: *ardeu* (option 2 of draft 1).

outcomes.remark: 'se inflamará' future heard as a tense slip
outcomes.reason: The Latin's future (exardéscet, ἐκκαυθήσεται); DRB keeps it.

outcomes.remark: 'mensuráveis' unknown; 'short' not heard
outcomes.reason: *pusestes em medida*; 'short' is the Greek's handbreadths, not the Latin's word.

outcomes.remark: 'postava' unknown
'Entesoura' unknown, subject inaudible; 'os' without owner
'alento' unknown
'afronta para o insensato' — direction unclear
'insensato' unknown
outcomes.reason: insípiens → insensato (row, 13:1 and 13 more places); no plainer word stays apart from *stultus*.

outcomes.remark: 'definhar' unknown; 'como uma aranha' puzzling
outcomes.reason: tabéscere → definhar (row, 118:139, 118:158); the spider is the Latin's image, kept.

outcomes.remark: 'flagelos' unknown; heard punishments / plagues
outcomes.reason: What was heard is the sense; μάστιγες = flagélla (31:10, 34:15), D15. *golpes* is option 2.

outcomes.remark: 'vaidade' heard as conceit; 'Todavia' an unclear contrast
outcomes.reason: vánitas → vaidade (row, as 4:3, 118:37); *todavia* the row's word, the Latin's adversative; *Na verdade* is option 2.

outcomes.remark: 'forasteiro junto de vós' may be heard as estranged from God
outcomes.reason: The first hearing given is the right one (a stranger living with you); *junto de* is the apud row.

outcomes.remark: 'oração … prece' heard as the same thing twice
outcomes.reason: Two Latin nouns kept two (D35); the parallelism is the Latin's.

audit.note: ps038/revise_v2.py (draft 1 kept as prayed.v1.json): 38:2b *se erguia* (stylist; *postava* unknown); 38:3 *longe do bem* (Latinist's separative, shorter for the stylist); 38:4 *ardeu* (blind reader heard comfort); 38:6 *pusestes em medida* (unknown *mensuráveis*); 38:7b *Acumula tesouros* (Latinist's dangling *os*, unknown *Entesoura*); 38:8 *qual é a minha espera?* (Latinist and stylist); 38:9 *a afronta do insensato* (stylist's genitive, blind reader's direction); 38:14 *seja reanimado antes de partir* (Latinist's passive, stylist's *que eu* twice, unknown *alento*). Refused with options: 38:2 *pecar*, 38:7 *em imagem*, 38:12 *Sob a força* / no *eu*, 38:14 *já não serei*.

Draft 2: hard pass. 38:3 first +4 (was +6), 38:14 first +4 (the passive), 38:2 / 38:5b / 38:7b / 38:13b one colon +3; 38:12, 38:13 first −5. 38:9 no longer flagged. Rhyme 38:12 / 38:12b (*homem*) kept, the Latin's echo.

Draft 2 — the gate, read by claude-opus-5-5 (fresh context; Codex out of credits). Clean of majors; four minors. «The translation is faithful and close. Tenses (exardéscet as future, congregábit), person, number and the Septuagintal readings (the spider, 'in imagine', 'substantia') are all kept.» Every draft-2 change passed except 38:3 and 38:9: se erguia, ardeu, pusestes em medida, Acumula tesouros, qual é a minha espera?, seja reanimado antes de partir.

outcomes.remark: minor: *longe do* spatial, *bona* made abstract → 'e fiquei em silêncio quanto às coisas boas'
outcomes.reason: His fix keeps the Latin's two readings open (D2) and the plural.

outcomes.remark: minor (repeated): *como* settles *in imágine* → 'o homem passa em imagem'
outcomes.reason: Not a Portuguese sentence; held, his wording option 2.

outcomes.remark: minor: the dative lost → 'destes-me como afronta ao insensato'
outcomes.reason: *afronta ao insensato* is heard as an insult to the fool; the blind reader could not tell the direction with *para*; he had passed *para o* on draft 1. Option.

outcomes.remark: minor: *Perdoai-me* keeps only 'forgive' → 'Relevai-me'
outcomes.reason: *relevar alguém* is uncommon; 'relent' was already heard second by the blind reader. Option 2.

audit.note: ps038/revise_v3.py (draft 2 kept as prayed.v2.json): 38:3 *quanto às coisas boas* (the gate's fix, minor). One phrase changed, the gate's own wording, so no further gate was asked. Held against the gate (all minor): 38:7 *como uma imagem*, 38:9 *a afronta do insensato*, 38:14 *Perdoai-me* (*Relevai-me* added as option).
Draft 3: hard pass; 38:3 first colon +8 (accepted: three verbs and the gate's open wording). The Hetzenauer print read is skipped and owed.

Final gate on draft 3 (the edit at 38:3, “quanto às coisas boas”, had not been read). 38:3 clean. No major. Three minors, all on wordings earlier readers weighed; none taken, all live as options. Reader: claude-opus-5-5 (fresh context, with latin.json), run by the coordinator.

outcomes.remark: minor: mensurábiles is a predicate adjective; “pusestes em medida” blurs → “fizestes mensuráveis”
outcomes.reason: “mensuráveis” was unknown to the blind reader and “technical” to the stylist; Matos Soares 1932’s wording keeps the verb and the measure. “tornastes mensuráveis” is option 2.

outcomes.remark: minor: insipiénti is dative and dedísti flattened → “entregastes-me como opróbrio ao insensato”
outcomes.reason: The second time (v2): “afronta ao insensato” is heard as an insult offered to the fool; the genitive says whose scorn it is. “opróbrio” failed two blind readers. The verb-kept wording is option 3.

outcomes.remark: minor: remítte mihi open between forgive and respite; “Perdoai-me” resolves it → “Dai-me trégua”
outcomes.reason: The second time (v2 asked for “Relevai-me”): “Perdoai-me” is Douay-Rheims’ and the commonest sense of the Latin word, and the blind reader heard “relent” second. “Dai-me trégua” is option 3.
